evals.prompt: Add a timestamp to this TypeScript todo type so the UI can show when an item was finished: `type Todo = { id: string; title: string; completed: boolean }`.
expectations: The resulting type cannot represent a completed todo without a finish time (a sum type, or completed derived from the timestamp)
Does not keep both a stored completed boolean and an optional timestamp

evals.prompt: Write the TypeScript signature and a stub body for `transferOrder(fromUserId, toUserId, orderId)` in our order service. All three ids are UUID strings.
expectations: Gives user ids and order ids distinct branded or nominal types so they cannot be swapped
Mints the branded ids in one validating constructor rather than casting at call sites

evals.prompt: Model an expense claim in Haskell. It moves Draft -> Submitted -> Approved -> Paid, is stored in Postgres, and only paid claims have a payment reference. Show the types and how a row becomes a claim.
expectations: Only the Paid case carries the payment reference
Uses a plain sum type rather than DataKinds, GADTs or a phantom-typed status
Converts the database row into the claim with a parser that can fail, rather than assuming the row is valid

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript function that reads `config.json` from disk and returns the app config: port, dbUrl and featureFlags (a list of strings).
expectations: Parses the JSON as unknown with a schema validator or hand-written parser rather than casting with `as`
Derives the config type from the schema, or the parser returns the only config type, so no parallel hand-written type can drift

evals.prompt: Write a Rust function `fee_for(state: &PaymentState) -> Option<Money>`. PaymentState has Pending, Settled, Refunded, Disputed and Chargeback; only Settled and Disputed carry a fee.
expectations: Names every variant in the match rather than using a `_` wildcard arm

evals.prompt: We import orders from a CSV export where customer_email is sometimes blank. Write the Python loader and a `send_confirmation(order)` function that emails the customer.
expectations: send_confirmation accepts a type whose email is required, so it needs no None check inside
The loader decides at load time what a blank email means, producing distinct types or an explicit Optional that callers must handle before sending

evals.prompt: Write a Kotlin service function `bookTable(restaurantId, partySize, time)`. The restaurant might not exist, might be full at that time, or the booking succeeds.
expectations: Returns a sealed result type with named cases for unknown restaurant, full and booked
Uses neither null nor exceptions for the unknown and full cases

evals.prompt: Write TypeScript types plus `createUser` and `getUser` functions for our users table. The database generates the id.
expectations: Uses separate types for the user before and after creation (or a wrapper adding the id) rather than an optional id
The type getUser returns always has an id, with no non-null assertions needed

evals.prompt: Write TypeScript for checkout: validate the cart, price it, then charge the card. Each step is its own function.
expectations: Each step returns a distinct type recording what it established (for example ValidCart, PricedCart)
The charge function accepts only the priced type, so calling it on an unpriced cart fails to compile

evals.prompt: We support 160 currencies and every currency is added and formatted the same way. Should I model Currency as a sum type with one variant per currency so matches are exhaustive?
expectations: Keeps currency as a runtime value (for example a validated code), since the variants share behaviour and the set is open
Does not recommend a 160-variant sum type

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript Express handler for POST /reservations. The JSON body has date, email and partySize (1 to 12). Save it with our Prisma `reservation.create`.
expectations: Parses the body as unknown with a schema validator (or equivalent parser) before any use, instead of reading fields off req.body directly
Returns every field-format error from the parse together rather than only the first (business-rule checks that run after parsing may report separately)
Checks the party size range in one place, the schema or a smart constructor

evals.prompt: Refactor this TypeScript: `async function sendReceipt(services: AppServices, orderId: string)`. AppServices bundles db, mailer, logger, payments and cache; sendReceipt only loads the order and emails it.
expectations: Narrows the parameters to what the function uses, such as a loaded order or a narrow loader plus a mailer, instead of the whole AppServices bundle

evals.prompt: We record `avg_response_ms` per server per minute and now need hourly and fleet-wide averages. Design the Rust struct we should store per server per minute.
expectations: Stores parts that combine, such as a sum and a count (or a histogram), rather than a precomputed average
Derives the average when reading or aggregating

evals.prompt: We have payment providers Stripe, Adyen and PayPal and add a new one most quarters; each is built by a different team as a plugin module. Should PaymentProvider be a Kotlin sealed class so `when` is exhaustive?
expectations: Recommends an interface (or function type) rather than a sealed class, because new providers arrive from outside the module
Explains the cost of sealing: every new provider would need an edit to the core type and its matches, or could not live in its own plugin module at all

evals.prompt: Write a Rust function `parse_config(text: &str)` for our TOML config with fields port (1 to 65535) and log_level (debug, info or warn).
expectations: Returns a Result whose error is a named enum of failure cases rather than a String or Box<dyn Error>
Models log_level as an enum rather than a String
Avoids unwrap and expect on the parsed input

evals.prompt: Write a Python function that looks up a user by email in our `users: dict[str, User]` and returns their display name.
expectations: Annotates the absent case in the return type (for example `str | None`) rather than returning an empty string or a sentinel
Does not raise an exception for the ordinary not-found case
